title: Dal Makhani
subtitle: Punjabi black lentil and kidney bean dal with cream and butter
excerpt: Whole black lentils and kidney beans slow-cooked overnight with tomatoes, ginger, and spices, then enriched with butter and cream. A Punjabi classic and the most celebrated dal in Indian restaurant cooking.

recipe.sourceNotes: Dal makhani is a Punjabi dish whose name translates to 'buttery lentils'. It was popularised in Delhi in the 1940s and 1950s by Kundan Lal Gujral, founder of the Moti Mahal restaurant, and his chef Kundan Lal Jaggi, who invented the tandoor for slow cooking large pots of dal overnight. The authentic dish uses whole black urad lentils and red kidney beans cooked for 8 to 12 hours on a very low heat, enriched with butter, cream, and tomato. The long cook is essential: the lentils must break down to create a thick, creamy consistency. A pressure cooker or overnight simmer achieves the same result at home.

recipeTools.notes: A heavy-based pan for the long simmer.

content.text: Soak the lentils overnight: unsoaked urad lentils take significantly longer to cook. The dal needs at least 2 to 3 hours of simmering to fully soften the lentils and break them down into a creamy consistency. Stir every 20 minutes and check the liquid level. The finished dal should be thick and velvety, not watery. The butter and cream go in at the very end: they should be stirred through off the heat so they enrich without splitting.

items.preparation: or whole urad dal, soaked overnight
dried, soaked overnight and cooked, or use a 400 g tin, drained

content.text: Drain and rinse the soaked lentils. Put in a large pan with 1 litre of fresh water. Bring to a boil and cook for 45 minutes until beginning to soften. Drain and set aside.

Heat the oil in the pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 12 minutes until golden. Add the garlic, ginger, and chilli. Cook for 3 minutes. Add the cumin, coriander, and paprika. Stir for 1 minute. Add the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.

Add the par-cooked lentils, kidney beans, and 600 ml of water. Season with salt. Bring to a simmer. Cook, partially covered, on the lowest heat for 1.5 to 2 hours, stirring every 20 minutes, until the lentils are completely soft and the dal is thick and creamy. Add water if it becomes too thick.
Stir in the butter and garam masala. Remove from the heat. Stir in the cream. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve with basmati rice and warm naan or roti.
